query: Who designed the Golden Gate Bridge?
answer: A team designed the bridge, not one person. Joseph Strauss was the chief engineer and usually gets the credit, but his first design, a clunky cantilever-suspension hybrid, was set aside [1][3]. Much of the actual engineering came from others. Leon Moisseiff developed the deflection theory behind the slender suspension design. Charles Alton Ellis did most of the detailed structural calculations. Ellis was fired in 1931, and his role wasn't formally recognized until 2007 [1][2]. The architect Irving Morrow gave the bridge its Art Deco towers and lighting, and he chose its "International Orange" color [1][4]. Clifford Paine also worked on the structural engineering. Construction ran from 1933 until the bridge opened in 1937 [1].
